notes: Documents: Honor Code page, CFCD Generative AI Statements page (both restrict, because of the EPC default ban 'Unless explicitly permitted by the instructor...') and the ITS Generative AI Usage Policy (permit). Both coders agreed on all three document stances. The Honor Code and CFCD pages repeat the EPC and Academic Affairs statements, so those units appear in both. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance, the most frequent split: A and B differed on neutral vs encourage/require/restrict/prohibit; resolved to neutral when the sentence only gives instructors or users a procedure, duty to verify, or communication task and takes no position on AI use, and to restrict (not prohibit) for Honor Code classification units because AI is allowed with instructor permission or acknowledgement. (2) Modality of the Honor Code classification sentences ('is a violation of the Honor Code', 'failure to do so is also a violation', plagiarism includes AI-generated content): A must/must-not, B informs; resolved informs since the ban itself is coded in the preceding unit. The 'Only Public information may be entered' unit resolved must-not (exclusive limit); the Appendix 'Sensitive Data can only be used in' unit resolved must-not/restrict. (3) policy_type: EPC default ban A P01 vs B P06 (resolved P01: states a default ban on submitted coursework, never mentions silence); 'Maximally restrictive policies should consider prohibiting' A P05 vs B P21 (P05: advice on the restrictive end of the range, not a student debug ban); 'Do not rely solely on the results of an AI detection tool' A P39 vs B P69 (P39); 'students need clarity ... in each course' A P66 vs B P09 (P09: justifies syllabus statements, asks for no discussion); ITS data rules Sensitive-data sentence A P92 vs B P50 and Restricted-data sentence A P50 vs B P80 (P50 both, consistent with the Public and Restricted data sentences). (4) phase/actor single splits: EPC ban general vs during-work (during-work); 'detail how and what uses of AI tools are appropriate' before-course vs course-start (course-start); 'Maximally encouraging policies should instruct students to cite' and 'GenAI may hallucinate' before-course vs course-start/general (before-course, policy design); library resource pointer and LLM-uses sentence actor (instructor for the resource pointer, all for the factual LLM-uses sentence). Only-A units kept (9): Honor Code sanctions list (actor changed to admin), preponderance-of-evidence standard, course-level discretion, student duty to clarify with instructor, second pledge sentence; CFCD 'various forms of AI have long been part of academic life', separate detection-metrics request, 'reconsider learning goals'; ITS 'tools that integrate into Wesleyan systems require ITS review'. Only-B units kept (7): Honor Code and CFCD adoption date (P84), GenAI benefit and threat rationale, 'appropriate use varies across disciplines', 'students need clarity' (set to phase general), CFCD library citation pointer. Nothing was dropped; B's second-pass units were genuine sentences in the source. B topic codes outside the starter codebook were mapped to it. new_types empty on both sides; no fit_note or uncovered_note was dropped (merged as 'A: ... B: ...' where both existed). No school, computing or course documents (course layer deferred in the collect file).
